principles.text: No new shorts into a gap-down that is extended from the MAs and lands on support (prior swing high, daily 50 EMA; Russell at the weekly 21). Wait for sideways action or a weak bounce into DECLINING MAs; step one is a failed push up that closes with a long upper wick. 10 Sep = observe-only day, flat, despite being bearish.
Gap-up and strong follow-through days in a CHOPPY market are the trap: they look like the next leading theme, but those names are the best short opportunities (IONQ rejection of the weekly EMAs).

Correction signature: a quick flush after a choppy stretch with DECLINING breadth - fewer stocks above their EMAs, EMAs flipping from support to resistance, names losing the weekly 9. SPY and IWM weakness confirms it.

Drawdown-conditioned breadth of exposure: in a drawdown from highs he shorted one quantum name instead of all three; outside a ~20% drawdown he would have taken all three. Protecting the downside while red beats maximising the idea.
Within a weak group, short the most liquid name with the weakest CLOSE - even if its daily chart is the strongest of the group (IONQ over RGTI/QBTS).

Anchored-VWAP short: anchor where price has visibly respected the line (e.g. the huge green pin bar / undercut rally, the all-time or swing high); short the rally into it and the failed reclaim, on a 1-min breakdown.

Stack resistance for a short: unfilled gap level + prior swing highs with long wicks + declining daily 50 + anchored VWAP + declining weekly 9/21. Plan it days ahead and take it even while the group is strong - trust the plan.
A short is more favourable when the rising 9 is still under the rising 21 and price is extended above them: the nearest support is far from the entry.
Express a sector short through the name that matches the weak index: a small-cap semi (AXTI, <$5B) when the Russell is the weakest index (lower highs, declining 9/21).
Hold a short through 1-2 hours of sideways action as long as it has not failed (reclaimed) the anchored VWAP from the swing high - the anchor, not the elapsed time, decides.

Extended-hours entries (mostly liquid commodities and crypto) use a stop-limit that is live in extended hours; after the open he switches it to regular-hours only (admits the sample is too small to know which is better). Extended-hours stop distance = the entry candle's high/low or the previous candle's.

Wait for great entries - not bad ones and not even fair ones. Getting in early is his recurring, expensive mistake; sitting out a day (Tuesday) cost him the IONQ re-entry, and he calls that price 'absolutely worth it'.
Trade journal = entry date, price, shares, exits, % gain/loss and total $ P&L. Simple and consistent.
SK Hynix's US ADR (SKHY) trades at a ~40-45% premium to the Korean share; FX, fees, liquidity and compliance explain part of it, but he thinks the premium is too high (a short-side consideration).
